what: sweep mode (flatten the playing memory in place, then put it back) — first live rig verification
where: car, amplifier attached, DSP powered, bridge http://127.0.0.1:8585, rta 8586
page: web/index.html, the new flatten-in-place module (SWEEP = {on,busy,snap,err,pct}); the old memory-select module was still resident in one stale browser tab and produced the accidental control below

accidental_control_old_page.note: A stale tab running the PRE-EDIT code (memory-select design) was clicked by mistake. It is a second live demonstration of section 37's finding, and it exposed a real fault that the new code has fixed.

steps.action: POST /api/master mute=true (to make the test silent)
old page: press Sweep mode -> read memory 4, then cmd 12 mem=3 mainDb=-8
old page: press Sweep mode again -> cmd 12 mem=1 mainDb=-3 (its own 'home')

findings: The LEVEL from the cmd 12 frame lands (-3 -> -8 -> -3). The MEMORY never moves: /api/status reports mem=1 throughout, while the old page's own check read /api/info (the bridge mirror) and reported 'on - memory 4 flat'.

The old sweepSwitch carried the page's cached mute flag, so it UNMUTED the car as a side effect (mute true -> false) even though nothing in the design intended a mute change. The new sweepSwitch reads /api/status first and echoes the device's own mute/groups/source/mem, so only mainDb changes.

verified_cycle.preconditions: device muted for the whole test (mute=true confirmed by /api/status); nothing audible
verified_cycle.tune_gate_during_sweep_mode: flat - 9 paths at 0 dB (the neutral verdict; baseRead reads the live memory)
verified_cycle.snapshot: localStorage ds18.sweepSnap = 23932 bytes (17 cells x 31 bands, fc/gain/q, plus byPass)

restore_comparison.crossovers: every scalar (lowFc, highFc, lowSlope, highSlope, lowFilterType, highFilterType) compared per path
restore_comparison.verdict: PASS - every band (fc/gain/q), every byPass bit, every crossover scalar and the master state are identical

conclusions: Flatten-in-place works: 17 cmd 14 writes, verified by 17 readbacks, with an independent device read confirming 0.00 dB on every path that carried EQ.
The restore works: 17 writes from the snapshot, verified by 17 readbacks, and independently confirmed byte-identical (527 bands + all crossover scalars + byPass + master state).
The memory never moved, as section 37 says - and it did not need to: the flatten landed in the memory that was already playing.
sweep mode's level write no longer carries page-cached mute/groups/source; it reads the device first. Confirmed: mute stayed true across the whole cycle.

Not covered by this test: audio (the cycle was muted throughout), the flush of a real sweep through a driver, the tune gate's 'tuned' verdict during a real capture, and the cmd 11 mute vector (no run was started).
